## General provisions of the chapter on validity (art. 3.1.1–3.1.4)

Source units: PICC_ART3_1_1_EN, PICC_ART3_1_2_EN, PICC_ART3_1_3_EN, PICC_ART3_1_4_EN.

| `valid-without-further-requirement` | Does the mere agreement of the parties suffice to conclude, modify or terminate the contract (art. 3.1.2)? | truth | `valid_without_further_requirement(c: Contract)` | `evaluate truth(valid_without_further_requirement(c: <c>));` | — | tests 1 |
| `validity-unaffected` | Do initial impossibility and the lack of a right to dispose affect the validity of the contract (art. 3.1.3)? | truth | `validity_unaffected(c: Contract)` | `evaluate truth(validity_unaffected(c: <c>));` | Article 3.1.3(1). The mere fact that at the time of the conclusion of the contract the performance of the obligation assumed was impossible does not affect the validity of the contract (`InitialImpossibilityDoesNotAffectValidity`); Article 3.1.3(2). The mere fact that at the time of the conclusion of the contract a party was not entitled to dispose of the assets does not affect the validity of the contract (`NoRightToDisposeDoesNotAffectValidity`) | tests 1 |

- **Does not answer:** What does the 1980 UN Convention answer on the validity of the contract? — the source delegates outwards (PICC_ART3_1_2_EN). HERE THE CONVENTION IS SILENT BY ITS OWN DECLARATION: article 4(a) takes the validity of the contract and of its provisions out of its subject matter. Chapter 3 of the Principles answers where the Convention declines to, and in substance there is no bridge between them.
- **Does not answer:** Does the party have capacity and what follows from its incapacity? — the source delegates outwards (PICC_ART3_1_1_EN). THE CHAPTER DOES NOT DEAL WITH CAPACITY (article 3.1.1): the conditions of a party's capacity are a question of the applicable law and an input of the case. The model answers this with a boundary rather than a conclusion.

A party may avoid the contract when it has been led to conclude it by the other party's fraudulent representation or fraudulent non-disclosure (`AvoidanceForFraud`); Article 3.2.7(1). A party may avoid the contract if at the time of its conclusion the contract unjustifiably gave the other party an excessive advantage (`AvoidanceForGrossDisparity`); Article 3.2.6. A party may avoid the contract when it has been led to conclude it by the other party's unjustified threat which is so imminent and serious as to leave no reasonable alternative (`AvoidanceForThreat`); Article 3.2.9. If the party entitled to avoid confirms the contract after the period for giving notice has begun to run, avoidance is excluded (`ConfirmationExcludesAvoidance`); Article 3.2.8(1). Where the ground is imputable to a third person for whose acts the other party is responsible, the contract may be avoided under the same conditions (`ThirdPersonForWhomPartyIsResponsible`); Article 3.2.8(2). Where the ground is imputable to a third person for whose acts the other party is not responsible, the contract may be avoided if that party knew or ought to have known of it (`ThirdPersonOutsideResponsibility`) | tests 2 |

A party may not avoid the contract where the risk of mistake was assumed or should be borne by it (`AssumedRiskBarsAvoidance`); Article 3.2.2(1)(a). A party may avoid the contract for a mistake of decisive importance where the other party made, caused or knew of the mistake and it was contrary to fair dealing to leave the party in error (`AvoidanceForMistakeKnownToOtherParty`); Article 3.2.2(1)(b). A party may avoid the contract for a mistake of decisive importance where the other party had not at the time of avoidance reasonably acted in reliance on the contract (`AvoidanceForMistakeWithoutReliance`); Article 3.2.2(2)(a). A party may not avoid the contract if it was grossly negligent in committing the mistake (`GrossNegligenceBarsAvoidance`); Article 3.2.10(2). Where the right to avoidance is lost, the party may no longer avoid the contract for mistake (`LostRightDefeatsMistakeAvoidance`); Article 3.2.4. A party is not entitled to avoid the contract on the ground of mistake if the circumstances afford, or could have afforded, a remedy for non-performance (`RemedyForNonPerformanceBarsAvoidance`) | tests 1 |

- **Does not answer:** Is the mistake material, is the threat imminent and is the advantage excessive? — data the case must bring (PICC_ART3_2_2_EN, PICC_ART3_2_6_EN, PICC_ART3_2_7_EN). THE EVALUATIVE ELEMENTS OF CHAPTER 3 GO THROUGH THE §47.3 JUDGMENT CHANNEL with the organ `Tribunal`: whether a reasonable person would have made the mistake material (3.2.2), a departure from reasonable commercial standards of fair dealing (3.2.2), the imminence and gravity of a threat (3.2.6), an excessive and unjustified advantage (3.2.7), a reasonable time for notice (3.2.12), the unreasonableness of upholding the remaining contract (3.2.13), a reasonable allowance in money (3.2.15), the reasonableness of remedies and of restitution in the case of illegality (3.3.1, 3.3.2). The model neither decides them nor substitutes a guess.

- **Does not answer:** Which rule of the applicable law is mandatory and what does it prescribe on infringement? — the source delegates outwards (PICC_ART3_3_1_EN). THIS IS NOT THE LAW OF A STATE. The Principles apply when the parties have agreed on them, or when a court or arbitral tribunal takes them as general principles of law; they do not replace the mandatory rules of the applicable law (article 1.4, hub `unidroit.picc`).
- **Does not answer:** Does the infringed rule prescribe the effects for the contract itself? — the source delegates outwards (PICC_ART3_3_1_EN). WHICH RULE IS MANDATORY AND WHAT IT PRESCRIBES IS AN INPUT OF THE CASE: article 3.3.1 refers to the infringed rule itself, and the Principles step in only where it is silent. Neither the list of such rules nor their effects is carried into the model.
- **Does not answer:** Which other factors are taken into account in assessing the reasonableness of a remedy? — data the case must bring (PICC_ART3_3_1_EN, PICC_ART3_2_7_EN). THE LISTS OF FACTORS IN ARTICLES 3.2.7 AND 3.3.1 ARE NOT EXHAUSTIVE ("among other factors", "in particular"): the seven criteria of article 3.3.1(3) and the two factors of article 3.2.7 are named in the request for a judgment rather than spread into separate premises — otherwise the model would pass off its own completeness as the rule.
